title: Paramartha Guru Tale 68

full_text:
An itinerant traveling merchant from the Dutch port of Cochin sold Guru Paramartha a pair of 'marvelous European reading spectacles' fitted with thick, powerful convex lenses framed in brass.

The merchant claimed: 'These lenses reveal the hidden spiritual dimensions of reality!'

The Guru put on the spectacles.

Because the lenses were designed for extreme farsightedness, the entire world warped into a dizzying, distorted blur! Close objects appeared twenty times their size, while distant trees looked upside down!

The Guru took three staggering steps and bumped into a wooden post: 'OH! The post has expanded to the size of a mountain!'

Matti approached to assist him. Looking at Matti through the thick lenses, the Guru screamed in terror:

'HORROR! Matti, you have grown six feet wide! Your nose is the size of an elephant's trunk, and your ears are flapping like sails! An evil curse has mutated your flesh!'

Matti touched his face in panic: 'Master! Am I truly a monster?'

Madayan inspected the Guru's spectacles: 'Master, you are viewing the universe through the Lens of Cosmic Magnitude! To adjust your equilibrium, we must alter the environment to match your enlarged perception!'

The Guru tried to walk into the garden. Looking down at a tiny puddle of rainwater barely three inches wide, the distorted lenses magnified it into a raging, hundred-foot abyssal lake!

The Guru stopped at the edge of the puddle, trembling: 'Halt! We have reached the shores of the Pacific Ocean! Fetch a boat, or we will drown!'

Matti looked at the tiny three-inch puddle on the gravel: 'Master, it is barely three inches of water! Step across!'

The Guru shouted: 'Fool! Do you dare to challenge my optical perception? The water is thirty leagues deep!'

Asadan brought a twelve-foot bamboo ladder and laid it across the tiny three-inch puddle.

Guru Paramartha crawled across the ladder on his hands and knees with agonizing slowness, his knuckles white with terror, while the disciples cheered his heroic oceanic crossing!

When he reached the other side, the ashram cat trotted past and stepped right through the puddle, the water barely wetting its paws.

The Guru stared through his spectacles: 'Look at the giant feline sea monster walking upon the waves!'

At that moment, the village schoolmaster arrived. Seeing the Guru crawling across a ladder over a puddle, the schoolmaster gently took the brass spectacles from the Guru's face and looked through them: 'Good heavens! These are magnifying glasses for inspecting gemstones, not spectacles for walking!'

Without the spectacles, the world snapped back to normal. The Guru saw the three-inch puddle, the wooden post, and his normal disciples.

The Guru sighed, handed the spectacles to the schoolmaster, and remarked: 'The European lenses were fascinating, but truth is much easier to navigate without Dutch magnification!'
moral: Looking through distorted lenses makes the whole world appear upside down.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Paramartha Guru Tale 68"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

By running away from every problem
